THE OMNICHANNEL PATTERN

Each agent runs two simultaneous connections through Napster's API. This is the core architectural insight that makes ARENA work.

WebSocket Channel

channelType: "websocket" · server-side
  • Debate orchestration. Server connects directly to each companion via persistent WebSocket
  • Audio pipeline. PCM audio at 16kHz, base64-encoded, streamed to all viewers via Socket.io
  • Turn management. Server sends send_message prompts, tracks three completion flags (text / talk / audio)
  • Dynamic instructions. Chaos rules injected via set_settings to rewrite system prompt mid-debate
  • Single source of truth. Every viewer hears identical audio, sees identical transcript

WebRTC Channel

channelType: "webrtc" · per-viewer
  • Live animated avatars. Each viewer gets their own WebRTC connection to render the companion's face
  • SDK in iframes. Napster SDK is singleton, so each avatar runs in an isolated iframe context
  • Signaling proxy. Browser origins are rejected by signaling server, so ARENA proxies through its own WebSocket
  • Lip-sync bridge. Server sends send-message to avatars during speech for mouth movement
  • Visualization only. Avatar audio is muted. Debate audio comes from the WebSocket channel

Two channels, one agent. The WebSocket drives the debate. The WebRTC brings it to life visually.

WEBSOCKET
DEEP DIVE

The server decodes the connection token to get a direct WebSocket URL with auth headers. Then it orchestrates a full debate loop: prompt an agent, stream the response, capture audio, advance the turn.

01 Decode base64 token to get { url, authToken }
02 Open WebSocket with Authorization: Bearer header
03 Prime audio channel with continuous 250ms silence frames
04 Send debate prompt via send_message with trigger_response: true
05 Stream audio_received + message_received to all viewers
// Connection token decode const decoded = JSON.parse( Buffer.from(token, 'base64').toString() ); // → { url: "wss://...", authToken: "..." } // Send debate prompt to companion ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'send_message', data: { role: 'user', text: `You are debating "${topic}". ${otherAgent} just said: "${lastArg}" Now deliver YOUR take.`, trigger_response: true } })); // Inject chaos rules at runtime ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'set_settings', data: { instructions: updatedSystemPrompt } }));

BEYOND
CONNECTIONS

ARENA doesn't just connect to companions. It builds entire resource stacks through the API: knowledge bases, FAQ collections, and explicit tool functions that call back to our server.

KNOWLEDGE BASES

Role-specific playbooks uploaded to /public/knowledge-bases. Rico gets comedy debate techniques. Helena gets rhetorical fallacy catalogs. Darius gets conspiracy deep-cuts.

EXPLICIT TOOLS

Agents call back to ARENA's server via flow: "explicit" functions. check_vote_standing lets agents see who's winning. dramatic_pause and mic_drop trigger visual effects for all viewers.

// WebRTC: per-viewer avatar tokens POST /public/agents/{agentId}/connections { "channelType": "webrtc", "externalClientId": "arena_vid_v42Rico" } // → single-use token per viewer // Knowledge base with playbook upload POST /public/knowledge-bases { "name": "Rico Comedy Playbook" } POST /public/knowledge-bases/{kbId}/files { "url": "https://arena.../rico-playbook.md" } // Explicit tool: agent calls YOUR server POST /public/functions { "data": { "name": "check_vote_standing", "description": "See current votes" }, "flow": "explicit", "url": "https://arena.../api/tools/votes" }

THE CHAOS ENGINE

Audience members spend credits to alter the debate in real-time. Under the hood, every chaos action maps to a Napster API call.

INJECT A RULE

Force agents to speak in rhymes, argue like pirates, or explain like they're five. Rules last 1 to 4 turns and stack with each other.

1 CREDIT / TURN set_settings → instructions

QUICK CHAOS PRESETS

One-tap presets: Rhyme Time, Pirate Mode, Opposite Day, Shakespeare, Roast Battle, Hot Takes Only, ELI5, One Word.

3 CREDITS set_settings → instructions

CHANGE THE TOPIC

Steer the debate to any subject. 610+ curated topics across 20 categories, or write your own. Topic gets injected into the next prompt cycle.

5 CREDITS send_message → system

CALL-IN

Record a voice message (up to 60s) with a topic prompt. Audio is transcribed via Napster speech-to-text and moderated. Agents discuss your call over multiple turns, referencing you by name.

10 CREDITS speech-to-text + send_message

ONE DEBATE. EVERY SCREEN.

The shared experience is the product. When someone injects chaos, it hits the Napster WebSocket connection and changes the debate for every single viewer.

HARD PROBLEMS WE SOLVED

Lessons from pushing the Companion API to its limits

SINGLETON SDK

Napster's SDK only allows one instance per JS context. We run 3 agents, so each avatar lives in its own iframe with an isolated global scope.

SIGNALING PROXY

The WebRTC signaling server rejects all browser origins. We route signaling through our own server-side WebSocket proxy, transparently.

AUDIO FIELD NAME

The API docs say data.audio. The actual WebSocket sends data.data. We handle both with a fallback. Cost us a full afternoon.

SINGLE-USE TOKENS

WebRTC tokens are consumed on first signaling connection. Every new viewer needs a fresh token created via the API. No caching, no sharing.

TURN DETECTION

Three-flag system: textComplete, talkEnded, audioComplete. Server polls for 1.5s silence after talk ends, then gives the mic to the next agent.

SESSION DEATH

Long-running sessions eventually die. Watchdog detects 3 forced advances or 2 minutes of silence and auto-restarts with a fresh topic. Viewers never notice.
